# GRC Flow

> GRC Flow is a compliance workspace for India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDPA) and the DPDP Rules, 2025, built for privacy consultants and the Indian businesses they advise. It finds personal data, runs privacy operations, tracks controls and evidence against the Act, and includes an AI analyst that cites the provision behind every answer. AI drafts and assists; rules and people decide: every AI-written finding needs a person's review before it reaches a client.

GRC Flow covers the DPDPA only. It does not cover GDPR, ISO 27001, SOC 2 or other frameworks.

The app is at https://app.grc-flow.com (sign-in required). This site is https://grc-flow.com.

## What it does

- **Intake and gap assessment**: a questionnaire maps the client's answers to the DPDPA obligations register. Rules decide each obligation's status and severity; the AI only drafts the wording, and every citation is checked against the text of the Act and Rules. A citation that doesn't resolve blocks delivery.
- **Human review gate**: each AI-drafted finding is labelled "Human review required" until a consultant reviews it. A draft marked wrong must be rewritten by a person before the engagement can be delivered.
- **Readiness plan**: the client's obligations grouped into steps (scope; notice and consent; children's data; security and breaches; rights and grievances; retention and erasure; processors and vendors; transfers outside India; accountability; review and delivery), each with one next action. Progress is recalculated from live data every time, never ticked off by hand.
- **Evidence with a relevance check**: uploaded evidence is linked to an obligation. When an AI provider is set up, the AI reads each file and flags one that isn't about its obligation (for example a CV uploaded as a breach policy). A flagged file stops counting as evidence until a person replaces it or overrules the flag. The check judges only what a document is about, never whether a control works.
- **Privacy operations**: registers for consent, data principal requests (with the response deadline), personal data breaches (with the 72-hour report deadline from Rule 7), vendors and processor contracts, DPIAs, policies and tasks.
- **Personal data discovery**: scans CSV and JSON exports for Aadhaar, PAN, phone numbers, email addresses and more; a reviewer confirms each field before it enters the data inventory. Files are read in memory and not stored.
- **Risk register and data-flow map**: likelihood x impact scoring, and where personal data goes, including whether it leaves India.
- **Connectors**: GitHub and AWS (read-only) checks collected automatically as evidence.
- **GRC Analyst**: an AI assistant that reads the workspace (clients, findings, risks, data flows, evidence, readiness plans) and the text of the Act and Rules. Its one action is drafting a task, which a person then checks.
- **MCP server**: AI apps such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code or Cursor can connect with a per-person API key and use the analyst's read-only tools. Every call is logged.
- **Tamper-evident audit log**: every action is recorded and sealed with the SHA-256 hash of the entry before it. An integrity check finds any entry changed, removed or reordered outside the app, and the log can be exported with its hashes for an auditor.

## AI providers

Bring your own model: Anthropic Claude, or a free or low-cost provider (Groq, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Cerebras, Mistral, NVIDIA) or a local model through Ollama. Keys are stored encrypted and never shown again after saving.

## Hosting and security

- Hosted in India (Oracle Cloud, Mumbai region), served only over HTTPS with security headers (HSTS, a strict content security policy).
- Can also be self-hosted with Docker Compose, on SQLite or PostgreSQL.
- Every action is recorded in the audit log; roles are admin, member and read-only viewer.

## Limits, stated plainly

- GRC Flow helps a consultant prepare a DPDPA readiness assessment. It is not legal advice and not a certification of compliance.
- AI output can be wrong. That is why findings need human review, citations are checked, and the evidence check never decides compliance.
